name: Gay World Order
caption: An nWo-parody stable that debuted on EFW's 16 Dec 1997 card and held the US Tag Team Championship for under two weeks before losing it back to the Horsemen at the Season's Beatings PPV.
notes: Managed by Coach Dike (spelled 'Coach Dyke' in the same documents). Debut card, 16 Dec 1997: the tag team Sweet Stuff (Juicy Fruit and Butt-A-Cup) beat the Horsemen's Tiny and Stupendous Steve for the EFW US Tag Team Championship; the Jolly Gay Giant led the group's entrance and wrestled EFW's Dante to a double countout. Little Rich made his EFW debut on the 21 Dec 1997 card against Horsemen enforcer Ice Century, losing by submission; the same night's limousine vignette with Coach Dike supplies the group's own catchphrase ('When you're GWO, you're GWO... 4 Life!'). The Jolly Gay Giant entered the Season's Beatings PPV's ten-man battle royal, and Sweet Stuff lost the US Tag Team Titles back to the Horsemen the same night (29 Dec 1997, Stupendous Steve's MoonPlex on Butt-A-Cup).

name: Children of Darkness
caption: A stable of Kestral, Krypt, Pariah, Despair, AsH and their attendants Blaxe and DarqueAngel, first attested across two December 1998 broadcasts.
notes: First attested in this collection across the two 12 and 23 December 1998 'Extreme Monday Night' episodes; not named in any of this wing's own already-served 1997 pages. Kestral holds the EFW Extreme North American Championship; Krypt and Pariah are former co-holders of the EFW Extreme Six Man Championship; Despair and AsH pursue the EFW Extreme Television and World Titles respectively into Seasons Beatings 98. Internal tension runs through both episodes: Krypt voices doubts about the group's ruthless direction to Jerry Styles (12 Dec 1998), and Krypt and Pariah argue on camera after Pariah misses a tag match searching for a missing DarqueAngel, accidentally chair-shotting his own partner on his return (23 Dec 1998).
